sections.heading: Effect in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

claims.text: In patients with heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less, dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily added to recommended therapy reduced the composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death compared with placebo.

evidence.quote: we randomly assigned 4744 patients with New York Heart Association class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to receive either dapagliflozin (at a dose of 10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to recommended therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of worsening heart failure (hospitalization or an urgent visit resulting in intravenous therapy for heart failure) or cardiovascular death.

the primary outcome occurred in 386 of 2373 patients (16.3%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 502 of 2371 patients (21.2%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001)

claims.text: In the same trial, death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 9.6% of the dapagliflozin group and 11.5% of the placebo group, and death from any cause in 11.6% and 13.9%, respectively.

evidence.quote: Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98); 276 patients (11.6%) and 329 patients (13.9%), respectively, died from any cause (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.97).

claims.text: In patients with class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less, empagliflozin 10 mg once daily reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for worsening heart failure compared with placebo.

evidence.quote: we randomly assigned 3730 patients with class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to recommended therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for worsening heart failure.

a primary outcome event occurred in 361 of 1863 patients (19.4%) in the empagliflozin group and in 462 of 1867 patients (24.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001)

claims.text: In that trial the total number of hospitalizations for heart failure was lower with empagliflozin than with placebo.

evidence.quote: The total number of hospitalizations for heart failure was lower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001).

claims.text: In the two trials of reduced ejection fraction, the treatment effect was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of diabetes.

evidence.quote: Findings in patients with diabetes were similar to those in patients without diabetes.
The effect of empagliflozin on the primary outcome was consistent in patients regardless of the presence or absence of diabetes.

sections.heading: Effect in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction

claims.text: In patients with class II-IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of more than 40%, empagliflozin 10 mg once daily reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure compared with placebo.

evidence.quote: we randomly assigned 5988 patients with class II-IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of more than 40% to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to usual therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

a primary outcome event occurred in 415 of 2997 patients (13.8%) in the empagliflozin group and in 511 of 2991 patients (17.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.90; P<0.001)

claims.text: In that trial the effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure, and the total number of hospitalizations for heart failure was lower with empagliflozin.

evidence.quote: This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group.

The total number of hospitalizations for heart failure was lower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (407 with empagliflozin and 541 with placebo; hazard ratio, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.61 to 0.88; P<0.001).

claims.text: In patients with heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of more than 40%, dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily reduced the composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death compared with placebo.

evidence.quote: We randomly assigned 6263 patients with heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of more than 40% to receive dapagliflozin (at a dose of 10 mg once daily) or matching placebo, in addition to usual therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of worsening heart failure (which was defined as either an unplanned hospitalization for heart failure or an urgent visit for heart failure) or cardiovascular death, as assessed in a time-to-event analysis.

the primary outcome occurred in 512 of 3131 patients (16.4%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 610 of 3132 patients (19.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.92; P<0.001)

claims.text: In that trial worsening heart failure occurred in 11.8% of the dapagliflozin group and 14.5% of the placebo group, while the hazard ratio for cardiovascular death was 0.88 with a confidence interval that included 1.

evidence.quote: Worsening heart failure occurred in 368 patients (11.8%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 455 patients (14.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.91); cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05).

claims.text: In the two trials of mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction, the effects appeared consistent in patients with or without diabetes.

evidence.quote: The effects of empagliflozin appeared consistent in patients with or without diabetes.
results were similar in prespecified subgroups, including patients with or without diabetes

sections.heading: Combined evidence across the ejection fraction spectrum

claims.text: In a prespecified meta-analysis of DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or first hospitalisation for heart failure among 12 251 participants, with consistent reductions in both components.

evidence.quote: Among 12 251 participants from DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced composite cardiovascular death or first hospitalisation for heart failure (hazard ratio 0·80 [95% CI 0·73-0·87]) with consistent reductions in both components: cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00]) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·74 [0·67-0·83]).

claims.text: Across five trials of 21 947 participants, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of composite cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure, cardiovascular death, first hospitalisation for heart failure, and all-cause mortality.

evidence.quote: In the broader context of the five trials of 21 947 participants, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of composite cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure (0·77 [0·72-0·82]), cardiovascular death (0·87 [0·79-0·95]), first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·72 [0·67-0·78]), and all-cause mortality (0·92 [0·86-0·99]).

claims.text: Treatment effects on the primary endpoint were generally consistent across the 14 subgroups examined, including ejection fraction.

evidence.quote: Treatment effects on the primary endpoint were generally consistent across the 14 subgroups examined, including ejection fraction.

evidence.quote: The frequency of adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups.

evidence.quote: Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin.

evidence.quote: Uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin.

evidence.quote: The incidence of adverse events was similar in the two groups.

pages.title: SGLT2 inhibitors in chronic kidney disease

claims.text: In patients with chronic kidney disease, with or without type 2 diabetes, dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily reduced the composite of a sustained decline in estimated GFR of at least 50%, end-stage kidney disease, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes compared with placebo.

evidence.quote: We randomly assigned 4304 participants with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 25 to 75 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (with albumin measured in milligrams and creatinine measured in grams) of 200 to 5000 to receive dapagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo. The primary outcome was a composite of a sustained decline in the estimated GFR of at least 50%, end-stage kidney disease, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes.

a primary outcome event occurred in 197 of 2152 participants (9.2%) in the dapagliflozin group and 312 of 2152 participants (14.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.61; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.51 to 0.72; P<0.001; number needed to treat to prevent one primary outcome event, 19 [95% CI, 15 to 27])

claims.text: In that trial the hazard ratio for the composite of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for heart failure was 0.71, and death occurred in 4.7% of the dapagliflozin group and 6.8% of the placebo group.

evidence.quote: the hazard ratio for the composite of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for heart failure was 0.71 (95% CI, 0.55 to 0.92; P = 0.009). Death occurred in 101 participants (4.7%) in the dapagliflozin group and 146 participants (6.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.88; P = 0.004).

claims.text: The trial was stopped early on the recommendation of the independent data monitoring committee because of efficacy.

evidence.quote: The independent data monitoring committee recommended stopping the trial because of efficacy.

claims.text: In patients with chronic kidney disease at risk for progression, empagliflozin 10 mg once daily reduced the composite of progression of kidney disease or death from cardiovascular causes compared with placebo.

evidence.quote: We enrolled patients with chronic kidney disease who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of at least 20 but less than 45 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area, or who had an eGFR of at least 45 but less than 90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 with a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (with albumin measured in milligrams and creatinine measured in grams) of at least 200. Patients were randomly assigned to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or matching placebo. The primary outcome was a composite of progression of kidney disease (defined as end-stage kidney disease, a sustained decrease in eGFR to <10 ml per minute per 1.73 m2, a sustained decrease in eGFR of ≥40% from baseline, or death from renal causes) or death from cardiovascular causes.

progression of kidney disease or death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 432 of 3304 patients (13.1%) in the empagliflozin group and in 558 of 3305 patients (16.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.64 to 0.82; P<0.001)

claims.text: In that trial the rate of hospitalization from any cause was lower with empagliflozin, but there were no significant between-group differences for the composite of hospitalization for heart failure or death from cardiovascular causes, or for death from any cause.

evidence.quote: The rate of hospitalization from any cause was lower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.78 to 0.95; P = 0.003), but there were no significant between-group differences with respect to the composite outcome of hospitalization for heart failure or death from cardiovascular causes (which occurred in 4.0% in the empagliflozin group and 4.6% in the placebo group) or death from any cause (in 4.5% and 5.1%, respectively).

sections.heading: Canagliflozin in type 2 diabetes and nephropathy

claims.text: In patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease receiving renin-angiotensin system blockade, canagliflozin 100 mg daily reduced the composite of end-stage kidney disease, a doubling of the serum creatinine level, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes compared with placebo.

evidence.quote: we assigned patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease to receive canagliflozin, an oral SGLT2 inhibitor, at a dose of 100 mg daily or placebo. All the patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 30 to <90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and albuminuria (ratio of albumin [mg] to creatinine [g], >300 to 5000) and were treated with renin-angiotensin system blockade. The primary outcome was a composite of end-stage kidney disease (dialysis, transplantation, or a sustained estimated GFR of <15 ml per minute per 1.73 m2), a doubling of the serum creatinine level, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes.

The relative risk of the primary outcome was 30% lower in the canagliflozin group than in the placebo group, with event rates of 43.2 and 61.2 per 1000 patient-years, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.59 to 0.82; P = 0.00001).

claims.text: In that trial the canagliflozin group also had a lower risk of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke, and of hospitalization for heart failure, with no significant differences in rates of amputation or fracture.

evidence.quote: The canagliflozin group also had a lower risk of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.95; P = 0.01) and hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). There were no significant differences in rates of amputation or fracture.

to receive dapagliflozin (at a dose of 10 mg once daily) or matching placebo, in addition to usual therapy
to receive dapagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo

claims.text: In the chronic kidney disease trial, the known safety profile of dapagliflozin was confirmed.

evidence.quote: The known safety profile of dapagliflozin was confirmed.

claims.text: Empagliflozin was studied at a dose of 10 mg once daily in heart failure with an ejection fraction of 40% or less, in heart failure with an ejection fraction of more than 40%, and in chronic kidney disease.

claims.text: Canagliflozin, an oral SGLT2 inhibitor, was studied at a dose of 100 mg daily in patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease.

evidence.quote: we assigned patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease to receive canagliflozin, an oral SGLT2 inhibitor, at a dose of 100 mg daily or placebo

lint.note: The meta-analysis names SOLOIST-WHF among the five trials included, but no document in this set describes SOLOIST-WHF itself, so its design and results are not covered by any page.
The documents cover kidney outcomes for dapagliflozin, empagliflozin and canagliflozin, but no document compares these agents head to head, so no comparison page is written.
